01

Inventory that scans cleanly

Shared alignment between headers and cells, a purposeful search toolbar, and compact identity and policy metadata.

Applied changes

  • Matched header and cell gutters; removed the asset button’s extra inner padding.
  • Balanced column widths and aligned revisions to the right.
  • Added an inventory title with its count, and gave asset search a predictable width.
  • Showed format and policy as distinct tags; used compact owner controls that open the full identity, including issuer.
  • Kept horizontal table scrolling inside its container on small screens.
WHY

Uniform alignment makes relationships between headers and values easier to read. Long identity strings should remain accessible without taking space from every other column. The owner disclosure preserves the full principal rather than silently shortening the underlying value.

02

A column picker with room to work

A focused dialog replaces the cramped floating list. Results and the selection review share one surface on desktop.

Applied changes

  • Larger search field; searches both column paths and types.
  • Checkbox-style selection rows, readable paths, type tags, and nested-field counts.
  • Selection review with removable tags and a clear-selection action.
  • Visible result count, selected-only view, select-results and deselect-results actions.
  • An empty state with a reset action; arrow keys and Enter select results, Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger.
WHY

Multi-selection needs a clear relationship between available choices and selected items. A review panel makes large selections inspectable, while actions scoped to the current search let users work with subsets without disturbing unrelated fields.

03

Keep authoring context close

Rule summaries communicate their audience and scope. The schema stays available while editing, and rule creation stays within reach while scrolling.

Applied changes

  • Catalog, policy, revision, format, save state, audience, column counts, masks, and row-filter scope use compact tags.
  • Breadcrumb links have consistent size, spacing, hover states, and wrapping; the workspace address becomes a small context tag.
  • Added a searchable schema sidebar with expandable nested fields, types, and nullability; it collapses with focus restoration.
  • Replaced repeated Add actions with one sticky “New rule” action in the rules toolbar. It appends and opens a rule, focuses its name, and preserves order after save/reload. Rule footers retain duplicate and delete.
  • Aligned duplicate and delete actions, improved rule padding, and kept the save bar within reach while scrolling.
WHY

Tags separate identity, scope, and status so a collapsed rule remains informative. A schema reference reduces back-and-forth lookup. The toolbar makes creation belong to the rule list and stays reachable during long edits on desktop and mobile. Existing-rule actions stay in each footer. The save bar supports completing edits without another full-page scroll.

One persistent creation action

The first revision repeated Add rule in the toolbar and existing rule footers. The follow-up replaces both placements with one New rule action in a sticky toolbar. Duplicate and delete remain attached to each existing rule.

Expand in place; complete SSO sign-out

Nested schema fields

Previously, every expansion reset the virtual list to its first row. Children were expanded but moved outside the viewport. Expansion and collapse now retain list scroll, page position, and keyboard focus on desktop and mobile. Nested parent rows also preserve their indentation.

Provider sign-out

Previously, Sign out revoked only the app session. It now clears local state and cookies before navigating to the provider logout endpoint. Confirm Logout on the provider page to end SSO. A real disposable Keycloak check verified that the next sign-in asks for credentials.

The app does not retain ID tokens, so provider confirmation is expected. Existing Keycloak realms must register the exact UI origin under Valid Post Logout Redirect URIs; new realm imports include it.

04

Bulk selection with visible scope

Selection tools live inside the picker, next to their results and counts. Typed schema ancestry controls subtrees, including paths whose field names contain dots.

Exclude several fields or a subtree

Applied changes

  • Select multiple exclusions with the same searchable list.
  • Exclude nested subtrees; restore one child without losing sibling exclusions.
  • Review excluded paths and the allowed-column count before applying.
  • Keep “Select all” explicitly global; select and deselect search results remain scoped to the filtered set.
WHY

The former one-item dropdown hid the scale of the operation. A visible exclusion set and resulting count make the effect reviewable before it replaces the local selection.

Preview prefix matches before adding

Applied changes

  • Preview the number of matching schema leaves.
  • Explain that prefixes match the start of the path.
  • Preserve existing selections and prevent duplicate or overlapping additions.
  • Disable adding when the prefix is blank or has no matches.
WHY

A match count gives immediate feedback before a broad selection. The additive behavior is explicit, so prefix selection does not unexpectedly replace existing work.

05

The same workflow on a narrow screen

The dialog fits a 390 × 844 viewport. Search, the bounded list, result actions, selection count, and Done remain accessible without page overflow.

Applied changes

  • Single-column picker on mobile, with a compact toolbar and sticky completion footer.
  • Rule metadata and action groups wrap cleanly.
  • Schema reference moves above the rules when available width is limited.
  • Clear focus indicators, meaningful icon labels, and readable light/dark theme tokens.
WHY

The old absolute popup competed with the rule card and nearby actions. A contained dialog gives selection its own space. The desktop review pane is hidden on mobile; selections remain visible through checked rows, the count, selected-only filtering, and tags in the rule.

06

Research behind the choices

Primary references informed the implementation. The larger dialog, sidebar placement, and visual hierarchy are design choices for this workflow.

Carbon · Data tables

Use consistent component sizing and a dedicated toolbar for search and global controls. Applied to shared cell gutters, predictable search placement, deliberate column widths, and one collection-level rule creation action.

Read Carbon guidelines

PatternFly · Multi-selection

Checkbox selection, typeahead filtering, visible selection counts, and explicit bulk-selection scopes informed the unified picker and result actions.

Select patterns · Bulk selection

W3C · Modal dialogs

Move focus inside the dialog, contain its tab sequence, support Escape, and restore focus to the invoking control. Applied with the existing Mantine modal and labeled close controls.

Read WAI-ARIA dialog guidance

OpenID · RP-initiated logout

Revoking the app session alone does not end SSO. Redirect to the provider logout endpoint with the client ID and a registered return URI; confirmation is expected without an ID-token hint.

Read OpenID logout specification
